_comment: Vision confidence thresholds, approved Session 10 (Q4). Different jobs
need different precision: a misread description is a wrong sentence, but a
misread button is a click on the wrong thing.
Each value is the confidence BELOW which the action is not taken silently.
Between 'refuse_below' and the action's own threshold, ZUZZ asks the user
to confirm. Below 'refuse_below' it declines outright and suggests another
approach, because a wrong click is worse than no click.
All values are 0.0-1.0. This file is re-read on every vision call, so it is
editable without a server restart; that is the intended way to tune these
on real hardware, where the useful values will differ from any guess made
before a single screenshot has been taken.
These supersede the flat 70% single threshold in docs/PHASE_3_PLAN.md
(OccipitalLobe.find_element and the risk table), which assumed one number

click_or_form_fill.why: a wrong click acts on the wrong target

information_extract.why: a wrong fact is quoted as if it were read

describe_scene.why: a loose description is still a useful hint

ocr_text_read.why: OCR output is transcribed onward, so errors compound

on_refuse: decline and propose an alternative approach

_comment: Approved Session 10 (Q7): Moondream first, Tesseract as the second read.
Tesseract is only invoked when Moondream's confidence is under its OCR
threshold or its text looks garbled, so the common case stays one model.
fallback.on_disagreement: use the higher-confidence read and flag it to the user
fallback.on_total_failure: ask the user to type what they see
